one_line_contribution: A budget-matched re-examination of agent experience-memory: length-matched decoy and padding/truncation arms are used to argue that injected-token volume, not memory content, drives both the documented harm of memory injection and the reported gains of two published curation methods, with tuned-k raw retrieval (k=1) offered as the cheap replacement.
closest_prior_work: Two threats, and the proposal engages only one. (a) Named and handled: Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) owns the length-vs-signal disentangling method; the proposal's rebuttal — procedural, non-answer-bearing injected content has no signal-loss term — is legitimate and is the main reason a decomposition paper still has room. (b) Not named at all, and more dangerous: the in-context-learning demonstration literature. Min et al. 2022 (Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations) established that demonstration *content* (even ground-truth labels) contributes far less than format/distribution, and the standard k-saturation curves show most of the benefit of demonstrations arriving by the first one or two exemplars. Predictions 1 and 3 — 'relevance-independent harm' and 'content value saturates at one item' — are close to the agent-memory restatement of that result, and Cuconasu et al.'s The Power of Noise already shows irrelevant retrieved text can be non-harmful or helpful at fixed budget, which cuts directly at prediction 1's assumed direction. The Related Work cites Lost in the Middle and The Power of Noise for the distractor point but never the demonstration literature, so a reviewer will read the saturation claim as either unaware of, or quietly re-deriving, a known ICL result. What survives that critique is only the curation re-examination table, not the decomposition block.
strongest_objection: Three of the five headline predictions are equivalence claims stated at margins at or below the design's own minimum detectable effect, so they cannot be won with the proposed n. The plan states MDE ~4 percentage points at n=600 with 72-108 discordant pairs; prediction 2 asks that the relevant-vs-decoy offset be <3 points, prediction 5 asks that BudgetFirst land within 2 points of the best curation method, and prediction 4's 'ties within the noise floor' clause is a TOST at a +/-4-point margin. TOST at a margin equal to the two-sided MDE has essentially no power (a well-powered TOST at +/-4 needs roughly 3-4x the discordant pairs available here), and 'within 2 points' is simply not resolvable. The likely outcome is a table of inconclusive non-rejections presented as nulls — exactly the failure mode the parent track's own measurement standards were written to forbid, and the proposal elsewhere shows it knows this (it correctly refuses to read a non-significant McNemar as a null). Secondary but load-bearing: C8a is defined as raw top-k 'selected/truncated' to C7a's per-instance token count, which conflates two different baselines. Truncating ExpeL-style raw trajectories mid-episode yields malformed, dangling text; if C8a then ties C7a, that is equally consistent with 'truncation destroys what the budget saves' as with 'curation was a budget artifact.' Prediction 4, the actual contribution, rests on this arm.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-power the equivalence tests or abandon them: either raise E1 to roughly n=1500-2000 paired instances (buy it by cutting the Llama-3.1-8B tier, the second seed on C2u/C10, and E2, none of which carry a quantitative claim), or pre-register wider, honestly-justified TOST margins and stop advertising '<3 points' and 'within 2 points' as the falsifiable form. (2) Split C8a into C8a-items (reach the budget by dropping whole retrieved items) and C8a-trunc (reach it by truncating), and report both; the gap between them is the truncation artifact and it must be measured, not assumed away. (3) Add the reverse-direction match (see missing_baseline) so 'shorter is better' is separated from 'raw text mutilated to be short is worse'. (4) Move the fidelity gate off the 100-instance dev split — at n=100 the gate's own MDE is ~10 points, so it admits or rejects reimplementations essentially by noise, and its asymmetry is adverse: a weak reimplementation that passes on a lucky dev delta will then tie at matched budget and be scored as confirming the confound. Gate on the full test set at natural length, with a pre-registered CI-overlap criterion. (5) Fix the reference k to whatever each source paper actually deploys rather than to C1(7) throughout; a budget confound demonstrated against a k=7 raw baseline that neither MemHarness nor A-MEM uses is a straw comparison. (6) Cite and position explicitly against the ICL demonstration-saturation literature, and state what prediction 3 adds beyond it.
missing_baseline: The reverse-direction budget match: the curated output padded or expanded back up to the raw arm's token count (C7a and C7b rendered at C1(7)'s length with neutral filler). The plan matches raw *down* to curated but never curated *up* to raw, so it cannot distinguish 'curation's gain is the shorter budget' from 'truncating raw text is what hurts.' The proposal already invented exactly this control for the decomposition block (C4, padded-single) and then failed to carry it into the contribution block, which is where the paper's claim actually lives. Relatedly, the re-examination table has no pure-length reference at the curated budget — C4 exists only at C1(7)'s token count, so there is no 'boilerplate filler at C7a's length' arm to read the curated numbers against. A reviewer aware of the parent track will also ask for an equal-token optimized-instruction arm (a GEPA/MIPRO-style strategy prompt costing the same tokens as the memory injection), since the track's premise is that instructions and demonstrations compete for the same budget, and this proposal drops the optimizer side entirely.
preprint_collision: Above average in honesty and unusually specific — it names IDs, states the scoop scenario for the decomposition half, and admits the coverage limit (six queries, tool call limit hit) rather than asserting exhaustiveness. But it is thin on the one question that decides the contribution, and the thinness is not fixable by more queries: whether A-MEM or MemHarness already contain an appendix-level length-matched or fixed-token-budget ablation. The check flags this as the scenario that demotes the paper from 'correction' to 'systematization' and then does not go look — that requires reading those two papers, which the proposal was going to reimplement anyway. Coverage is also skewed: it searches 2026 agent-memory and long-context work and entirely misses the in-context-learning demonstration literature, which is where the saturation and relevance-independence predictions are most exposed (see closest_prior_work); a collision check that misses the strongest novelty threat has not established novelty for predictions 1 and 3. Finally, the entire contribution block depends on two preprints, one roughly two months old (arXiv 2607.28272), reimplemented from text with no released code — so the re-examination table risks being a re-examination of the proposal's own reconstruction of those methods. No named preprint makes this exact claim, so this is a weakness in the novelty argument rather than an actual collision.
